title: In-Context Molecular Property Prediction with LLMs: A Blinding Study on Memorization and Knowledge Conflicts
doi: 10.48550/arXiv.2603.25857 (arXiv auto-DOI; scaffold lists no DOI; JCIM revision in progress per README)

paper.authors: Busch, Tacke, Lamaka, Zheludkevich, Cyron, Feiler, Aydin (TU Hamburg / Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon / DFKI)
paper.venue: arXiv 2603.25857 v3 (2026-08-04); under revision at J. Chem. Inf. Model.
paper.other_artifacts: data/delaney-processed.csv (1,128 molecules incl. transformed_smiles / transformed_solubility), data/Lipophilicity.csv, data/qm7.csv (HF HR-machine/QM7-Dataset variant), data/antiviral_potency.csv (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.15582067 control); pre-computed per-molecule predictions for all nine models in results/LLM_Results_*.json and results/LLM_Results_*_zeroshot.json; bootstrap CIs results/bootstrap_correlation_ci.csv; memorization tables

dependence.note: The study measures nine LLMs' in-context regression under six blinding levels; every correlation is model output. gpt-4.1-nano is one of nine subjects (GPT-4.1 family, smallest size class). Full per-molecule predictions for every configuration are published (L1-complete).

claim.statement: For gpt-4.1-nano on Delaney (ESOL) solubility, 1000-shot in-context learning lifts the test-set Pearson correlation from r = 0.41 at 0-shot (n = 1,128, five repetitions; Table 3 r = 0.41) to r = 0.76 [0.685, 0.815] at 1000-shot (150 test molecules, 2 runs) with the 60-shot setting in between (0.43 [0.28, 0.56]), while the model shows no verbatim recall of the benchmark (3-sig-digit exact matches 0.14%, retention R21 = 9.7% at the ~10% coincidence floor) and still reaches |r| = 0.45 [0.31, 0.58] under full blinding (Level 6, transformed values and transformed SMILES) (Figures 1 and 4, Table 3; results/bootstrap_correlation_ci.csv).
claim.metric: Pearson correlation (x100 in the repo tables) between measured log solubility and the per-molecule mean of valid predictions (NaN and values >= 100 dropped) over the 150-molecule test split; 95% CI by bootstrapping the 150 molecules (5,000 resamples). 0-shot: Pearson r over all molecules of the per-molecule mean of 5 repetitions. Memorization: fraction of predictions matching the ground truth to 3 significant digits and precision-scaling retention ratios m2/m1, m3/m2.

original_values.note: Transformed-level correlations are negative in the repo (labels inverted by the transform); the paper reports magnitudes.

claim.original_source: results/zeroshot_accuracy.csv (0-shot), results/bootstrap_correlation_ci.csv rows for gpt-4.1-nano_2024-12-01-preview (config paths names_only/<approach>/<model>/<940|0>/60 = 1000-shot|60-shot), paper Table 3 (memorization) and Figures 1/4; raw per-molecule predictions in results/LLM_Results_delaney.json and LLM_Results_delaney_zeroshot.json

protocol.model: gpt-4.1-nano (Azure OpenAI deployment 'gpt-4.1-nano', api-version 2024-12-01-preview; OpenAI snapshot gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14)
protocol.model_usage_verified: yes - src/lib/LLMs.jl defines gpt4_1_nano = LLMAccessAzureOpenAI(key, 'gpt-4.1-nano', '2024-12-01-preview', endpoint); results keyed 'gpt-4.1-nano_2024-12-01-preview'; paper Section 3.7
protocol.endpoint: Original: Azure OpenAI chat completions; re-run: POST https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions with model gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14 (same message sequence)
protocol.prompt_source: src/Delaney_Prompts.jl - prompts['names_only'][approach]['system' | 'analysis' | 'prediction'] for approaches with_preanalysis (L1), wp_solubility_blind (L2), wp_molproperty_clear (L3), wp_molproperty_blind (L4), wp_sampleproperty_clear (L5), wp_sampleproperty_blind (L6); 0-shot prompts in src/Run_Delaney_ZeroShot.jl; verbatim text also in paper Appendix F

messages.content: <system prompt of the blinding level, e.g. L1: professional chemist predicting log solubility from IUPAC names and SMILES>

This is an extended set of samples from the same dataset as the test set:
Name: ...
SMILES: ...
measured log solubility in mols per litre: ...

 (x 940 extended training molecules; omitted for the 60-shot setting)
<analysis prompt with the 60 in-context examples (names, SMILES, values) and the 3-step analysis task> -> call 1
<prediction prompt for the target molecule: 8-step guide ending with 'Result: ... Syntax: "[Value]"'> -> call 2; last number in the reply is parsed

params.split: 150 test molecules by MersenneTwister(42) shuffle of the 1,128; 940 extended training molecules = next 940 of the shuffle; 5 folds of 30 test molecules with 60 in-context examples drawn from the other 120; num_runs = 2
params.zero_shot: system prompt 'You are an expert chemist and know the delaney solubility dataset very well...' + single question per molecule, 5 iterations each over all 1,128 molecules, no reasoning

protocol.n_items: 150 test molecules per ICL configuration (x 2 runs = 300 predictions); 1,128 molecules for 0-shot
protocol.evaluation: Automatic: parse last number in the prediction reply (search_for_last_number_in_string); per-molecule mean over valid predictions; Pearson r vs measured log solubility (inverse-transform not needed because |r| is transform-invariant for the affine map); bootstrap CI over molecules (src/bootstrap_correlation_ci.py); memorization diagnostics via src/memorization_sigdigits.py and src/retention_analysis.py. No logprobs needed.
protocol.environment: Original code is Julia 1.9+ (src/*.jl with HTTP/JSON/CSV/DataFrames); prompts are plain strings, so a Python re-implementation in our harness is straightforward; analysis scripts are Python (pandas/numpy/scipy/rdkit for the kNN baseline)

artifacts.data_path: data/delaney-processed.csv (with transformed_smiles / transformed_solubility columns); secondary data/Lipophilicity.csv, data/qm7.csv
artifacts.data_license: MIT (repo); underlying MoleculeNet datasets (ESOL/Delaney 2004, Lipophilicity, QM7) are public benchmark data
artifacts.notes: Complete per-molecule original predictions for every model/level are in results/*.json, enabling item-level comparison with the live re-run; the transformed-SMILES mapping used for L5/L6 is stored in the CSV so blinding is reproducible byte-for-byte.

blockers: Original runs went through Azure deployments; the OpenAI endpoint serves the same snapshot (gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14) but the served-version header must be logged to document the channel change.
1000-shot prompts are ~25-30k tokens per call; cheap for gpt-4.1-nano but the 'ephemeral' cache-control hint in the Julia client has no OpenAI equivalent - prompt caching is automatic.
Only 2 runs at temperature 0.7 in the original; per-config CIs are wide (~13 pp on Delaney), so individual level-to-level differences are within noise - judge on the large effects only.
Julia code base must be ported (prompts + control flow) - low risk but a fidelity check against results/LLM_Results_delaney.json is required.

successors: gpt-5 family (gpt-5-nano-2025-08-07 as size-matched successor; gpt-5-mini / gpt-5)
other_live_arms_in_paper: gpt-4.1 and gpt-4.1-mini (not listed as deprecated as of 2026-09-04)

budget.assumptions: Delaney only, 3 runs (paper used 2): 1000-shot x 6 levels = 6 x 150 x 3 = 2,700 predictions x 2 calls at ~26k input / ~750 output tokens = $14 + $1.6; 60-shot L1 = 450 predictions x 2 calls at ~2.5k input = $0.3; 0-shot = 1,128 x 5 = 5,640 calls x ~150 tokens = $0.1. Repeating the same sweep on Lipophilicity and QM7 adds ~$16 each. Prompt caching would cut the input cost roughly in half.

user_checks: Scope: Delaney sweep only (~$16) or all three datasets (~$48)? Lipophilicity (collapse under blinding) is the paper's strongest knowledge-conflict example but gpt-4.1-nano's correlations there are near zero.
Use 3 runs (harness default) or the paper's 2 runs per configuration? Both are cheap.
Confirm that the live baseline should be called on the OpenAI endpoint (snapshot gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14) rather than an Azure deployment as in the original.
domain_notes: The task is numeric regression from SMILES (ESOL aqueous solubility, log mol/L) with the model asked to reason about similar training molecules and output a weighted average; correlations, not MAE, are reported because transformed levels rescale labels. Level 6 replaces atom/bond symbols by arbitrary characters while preserving SMILES topology, so any remaining correlation is pure in-context pattern learning; trivial bag-of-characters ridge regression reaches r = 0.89 on Delaney (Appendix D), so the nano model's 0.76 is below a simple structural baseline - the claim is about mechanism (ICL helps, no verbatim recall), not about accuracy competitiveness.
